passages.text: I must go on boasting. Although there is nothing to gain, I will go on to visions and revelations from the Lord.
passages.sermon:
Paul is the speaker.
\r\nPaul says he must go on boasting.
\r\nBoasting does not benefit him.
\r\nPaul will continue.
\r\nHe will speak about visions from the Lord.
\r\nHe will speak about revelations from the Lord.
passages.original: Καυχᾶσθαι δεῖ οὐ συμφέρον μέν ἐλεύσομαι δὲ εἰς ὀπτασίας καὶ ἀποκαλύψεις Κυρίου

passages.text: I know a man in Christ who fourteen years ago was caught up to the third heaven. Whether it was in the body or out of it I do not know, but God knows.
passages.sermon:
Paul is the speaker.
Paul is a Christian apostle.
Paul says he knows a man who belongs to Christ.
This man had a special experience fourteen years ago.
God caught up this man to the third heaven.
Paul does not know if this happened in the body.
Paul does not know if this happened out of the body.
God knows how it happened.
passages.original: οἶδα ἄνθρωπον ἐν Χριστῷ πρὸ ἐτῶν δεκατεσσάρων εἴτε ἐν σώματι οὐκ οἶδα εἴτε ἐκτὸς τοῦ σώματος οὐκ οἶδα ὁ Θεὸς οἶδεν ἁρπαγέντα τὸν τοιοῦτον ἕως τρίτου οὐρανοῦ

passages.text: And I know that this man—whether in the body or out of it I do not know, but God knows— was caught up to Paradise. The things he heard were too sacred for words, things that man is not permitted to tell.
passages.sermon:
I know a man in Christ.
God knows whether this man was in the body or out of the body.
I do not know if he was in the body or out of the body.
This man was caught up to Paradise.
He heard words there that are too sacred to speak.
No person is allowed to say these things.
passages.original: καὶ οἶδα τὸν τοιοῦτον ἄνθρωπον εἴτε ἐν σώματι εἴτε χωρὶς τοῦ σώματος οὐκ οἶδα ὁ Θεὸς οἶδεν ὅτι ἡρπάγη εἰς τὸν Παράδεισον καὶ ἤκουσεν ἄρρητα ῥήματα ἃ οὐκ ἐξὸν ἀνθρώπῳ λαλῆσαι

passages.text: I will boast about such a man, but I will not boast about myself, except in my weaknesses.
passages.sermon:
Paul is the speaker.
\r\nPaul will boast about this man who was caught up to heaven.
\r\nPaul will not boast about himself.
\r\nPaul will only boast about his own weaknesses.
passages.original: Ὑπὲρ τοῦ τοιούτου καυχήσομαι ὑπὲρ δὲ ἐμαυτοῦ οὐ καυχήσομαι εἰ μὴ ἐν ταῖς ἀσθενείαις

passages.text: Even if I wanted to boast, I would not be a fool, because I would be speaking the truth. But I refrain, so no one will credit me with more than he sees in me or hears from me, or because of these surpassingly great revelations. So to keep me from becoming conceited, I was given a thorn in my flesh, a messenger of Satan, to torment me.
passages.sermon:
Paul is the speaker.
Paul is an apostle of Jesus Christ.
Paul received great revelations from God.
If I want to boast, I will not be foolish.
I will speak the truth.
But I hold back from boasting.
I do this so no one will think more of me than what he sees in me.
I do this so no one will think more of me than what he hears from me.
I do this because of the very great revelations I received.
God gave me a thorn in my flesh.
This thorn is a messenger of Satan.
This messenger torments me.
God allowed this so I would not become proud.
passages.original: ἐὰν γὰρ θελήσω καυχήσασθαι οὐκ ἔσομαι ἄφρων ἀλήθειαν γὰρ ἐρῶ φείδομαι δέ μή τις εἰς ἐμὲ λογίσηται ὑπὲρ ὃ βλέπει με ἢ ἀκούει τι ἐξ ἐμοῦ καὶ τῇ ὑπερβολῇ τῶν ἀποκαλύψεων Διὸ ἵνα μὴ ὑπεραίρωμαι ἐδόθη μοι σκόλοψ τῇ σαρκί ἄγγελος Σατανᾶ ἵνα με κολαφίζῃ ἵνα μὴ ὑπεραίρωμαι

passages.text: Three times I pleaded with the Lord to take it away from me.
passages.sermon:
Paul is an apostle of Jesus Christ.
Paul received great revelations from God.
Paul was given a thorn in his flesh to keep him humble.
This thorn was a messenger of Satan to torment him.
Paul did not want this suffering.
Paul pleaded with the Lord three times.
Paul asked the Lord to take the thorn away from him.
passages.original: ὑπὲρ τούτου τρὶς τὸν Κύριον παρεκάλεσα ἵνα ἀποστῇ ἀπ’ ἐμοῦ

passages.text: But He said to me, “My grace is sufficient for you, for My power is perfected in weakness.” Therefore I will boast all the more gladly in my weaknesses, so that the power of Christ may rest on me.
passages.sermon:
The Lord spoke to me.
He said, “My grace is enough for you.”
He said, “My power becomes perfect in weakness.”
Because of this, I will gladly boast about my weaknesses.
I do this so that the power of Christ may rest on me.
passages.original: καὶ εἴρηκέν μοι Ἀρκεῖ σοι ἡ χάρις μου ἡ γὰρ δύναμις ἐν ἀσθενείᾳ τελεῖται Ἥδιστα οὖν μᾶλλον καυχήσομαι ἐν ταῖς ἀσθενείαις μου ἵνα ἐπισκηνώσῃ ἐπ’ ἐμὲ ἡ δύναμις τοῦ Χριστοῦ

passages.text: That is why, for the sake of Christ, I delight in weaknesses, in insults, in hardships, in persecutions, in difficulties. For when I am weak, then I am strong.
passages.sermon:
Paul is an apostle of Jesus Christ.
Paul serves Christ faithfully.
Paul faces many troubles because of Christ.
Paul delights in his weaknesses.
Paul delights in insults.
Paul delights in hardships.
Paul delights in persecutions.
Paul delights in difficulties.
Paul does all this for the sake of Christ.
When Paul is weak, then he is strong.
passages.original: διὸ εὐδοκῶ ἐν ἀσθενείαις ἐν ὕβρεσιν ἐν ἀνάγκαις ἐν διωγμοῖς καὶ στενοχωρίαις ὑπὲρ Χριστοῦ ὅταν γὰρ ἀσθενῶ τότε δυνατός εἰμι

passages.text: I have become a fool, but you drove me to it. In fact, you should have commended me, since I am in no way inferior to those “super-apostles,” even though I am nothing.
passages.sermon:
Paul is an apostle of Jesus Christ.
Paul says, "I have become a fool."
You forced me to act this way.
You should have commended me.
I am not less than those so-called 'super-apostles.'
I am nothing on my own.
passages.original: Γέγονα ἄφρων ὑμεῖς με ἠναγκάσατε ἐγὼ γὰρ ὤφειλον ὑφ’ ὑμῶν συνίστασθαι οὐδὲν γὰρ ὑστέρησα τῶν Ὑπερλίαν ἀποστόλων εἰ καὶ οὐδέν εἰμι

passages.text: The true marks of an apostle—signs, wonders, and miracles—were performed among you with great perseverance.
passages.sermon:
Paul is an apostle of Jesus Christ.
Paul showed the true marks of an apostle among you.
He performed signs among you.
He performed wonders among you.
He performed miracles among you.
He did all these things with great perseverance.
passages.original: τὰ μὲν σημεῖα τοῦ ἀποστόλου κατειργάσθη ἐν ὑμῖν ἐν πάσῃ ὑπομονῇ σημείοις τε καὶ τέρασιν καὶ δυνάμεσιν

passages.text: In what way were you inferior to the other churches, except that I was not a burden to you? Forgive me this wrong!
passages.sermon:
You are not less than the other churches in any way.
There is only one difference.
I did not become a burden to you.
Please forgive me for this wrong.
passages.original: τί γάρ ἐστιν ὃ ἡσσώθητε ὑπὲρ τὰς λοιπὰς ἐκκλησίας εἰ μὴ ὅτι αὐτὸς ἐγὼ οὐ κατενάρκησα ὑμῶν χαρίσασθέ μοι τὴν ἀδικίαν ταύτην

passages.text: See, I am ready to come to you a third time, and I will not be a burden, because I am not seeking your possessions, but you. For children should not have to save up for their parents, but parents for their children.
passages.sermon:
Paul is an apostle of Jesus Christ.
Paul writes to the church in Corinth.
Paul says, “I am ready to visit you for the third time.”
I will not be a burden to you.
I do not want your possessions.
I want you.
Children do not have to save up for their parents.
Parents should save up for their children.
passages.original: Ἰδοὺ τρίτον τοῦτο ἑτοίμως ἔχω ἐλθεῖν πρὸς ὑμᾶς καὶ οὐ καταναρκήσω οὐ γὰρ ζητῶ τὰ ὑμῶν ἀλλὰ ὑμᾶς οὐ γὰρ ὀφείλει τὰ τέκνα τοῖς γονεῦσιν θησαυρίζειν ἀλλὰ οἱ γονεῖς τοῖς τέκνοις

passages.text: And for the sake of your souls, I will most gladly spend my money and myself. If I love you more, will you love me less?
passages.sermon:
Paul is an apostle of Jesus Christ.
Paul writes to the church in Corinth.
Paul cares deeply for their souls.
Paul says, "I will gladly spend my money for you."
Paul also says, "I will gladly give myself for you."
Paul does this for the sake of your souls.
Paul asks, "If I love you more, will you love me less?"
passages.original: ἐγὼ δὲ ἥδιστα δαπανήσω καὶ ἐκδαπανηθήσομαι ὑπὲρ τῶν ψυχῶν ὑμῶν εἰ περισσοτέρως ὑμᾶς ἀγαπῶν ἧσσον ἀγαπῶμαι

passages.text: Be that as it may, I was not a burden to you; but crafty as I am, I caught you by trickery.
passages.sermon:
Paul is speaking to the Corinthians.
\r\nPaul says he did not burden them.
\r\nSome people claim Paul acted with craftiness.
\r\nThey say Paul caught the Corinthians by trickery.
\r\nPaul denies being a burden.
\r\nPaul addresses the accusation of using deceit.
passages.original: Ἔστω δέ ἐγὼ οὐ κατεβάρησα ὑμᾶς ἀλλὰ ὑπάρχων πανοῦργος δόλῳ ὑμᾶς ἔλαβον

passages.text: Did I exploit you by anyone I sent you?
passages.sermon:
Paul is an apostle of Jesus Christ.
\r\nPaul sent people to visit the Corinthians.
\r\nPaul asks a question.
\r\nPaul says, "Did I take advantage of you through anyone I sent to you?"
passages.original: μή τινα ὧν ἀπέσταλκα πρὸς ὑμᾶς δι’ αὐτοῦ ἐπλεονέκτησα ὑμᾶς

passages.text: I urged Titus to visit you, and I sent our brother with him. Did Titus exploit you in any way? Did we not walk in the same Spirit and follow in the same footsteps?
passages.sermon:
I am Paul, an apostle of Jesus Christ.
I urged Titus to visit you.
I sent our brother with Titus.
Titus did not exploit you.
We walked in the same Spirit.
We followed the same footsteps.
passages.original: παρεκάλεσα Τίτον καὶ συναπέστειλα τὸν ἀδελφόν μήτι ἐπλεονέκτησεν ὑμᾶς Τίτος οὐ τῷ αὐτῷ Πνεύματι περιεπατήσαμεν οὐ τοῖς αὐτοῖς ἴχνεσιν

passages.text: Have you been thinking all along that we were making a defense to you? We speak before God in Christ, and all of this, beloved, is to build you up.
passages.sermon:
Paul is speaking to the Corinthian believers.
Paul asks if they think he has been making a defense to them.
Paul says he speaks before God.
Paul says he speaks in Christ.
Paul says everything he does is for their benefit.
Paul calls them beloved.
Paul says his purpose is to build them up.
passages.original: Πάλαι δοκεῖτε ὅτι ὑμῖν ἀπολογούμεθα κατέναντι Θεοῦ ἐν Χριστῷ λαλοῦμεν τὰ δὲ πάντα ἀγαπητοί ὑπὲρ τῆς ὑμῶν οἰκοδομῆς

passages.text: For I am afraid that when I come, I may not find you as I wish, and you may not find me as you wish. I fear that there may be quarreling, jealousy, rage, rivalry, slander, gossip, arrogance, and disorder.
passages.sermon:
Paul is writing to the church in Corinth.
Paul is an apostle of Jesus Christ.
Paul cares about the believers in Corinth.
Paul says, “I am afraid.”
Paul fears what he will find when he visits them.
Paul says, “When I come, I may not find you as I wish.”
Paul wants to find them living rightly.
Paul says, “You may not find me as you wish.”
Paul fears disappointment on both sides.
Paul fears there may be quarreling among them.
Paul fears there may be jealousy among them.
Paul fears there may be outbursts of anger among them.
Paul fears there may be rivalry among them.
Paul fears there may be slander among them.
Paul fears there may be gossip among them.
Paul fears there may be arrogance among them.
Paul fears there may be disorder among them.
passages.original: φοβοῦμαι γὰρ μή πως ἐλθὼν οὐχ οἵους θέλω εὕρω ὑμᾶς κἀγὼ εὑρεθῶ ὑμῖν οἷον οὐ θέλετε μή πως ἔρις ζῆλος θυμοί ἐριθεῖαι καταλαλιαί ψιθυρισμοί φυσιώσεις ἀκαταστασίαι

passages.text: I am afraid that when I come again, my God will humble me before you, and I will be grieved over many who have sinned earlier and have not repented of their acts of impurity, sexual immorality, and debauchery.
passages.sermon:
Paul is an apostle of Jesus Christ.
\r\nPaul writes to the church in Corinth.
\r\nPaul fears what will happen when he visits them again.
\r\nPaul says, “I am afraid that when I come again, my God will humble me before you.”
\r\nPaul expects to feel sorrow.
\r\nPaul will grieve over many people.
\r\nThese people sinned earlier.
\r\nThey have not repented.
\r\nThey committed acts of impurity.
\r\nThey committed sexual immorality.
\r\nThey acted with debauchery.
passages.original: μὴ πάλιν ἐλθόντος μου ταπεινώσῃ με ὁ Θεός μου πρὸς ὑμᾶς καὶ πενθήσω πολλοὺς τῶν προημαρτηκότων καὶ μὴ μετανοησάντων ἐπὶ τῇ ἀκαθαρσίᾳ καὶ πορνείᾳ καὶ ἀσελγείᾳ ᾗ ἔπραξαν
